summary.title: Augmented reality with Python and OpenCV (part 1)
summary.one_liner: You learn how a planar-marker augmented reality pipeline works: feature detection and matching with ORB, then estimating a homography with RANSAC in OpenCV.
keywords: how to recognize a flat object in an image
takeaways: Object recognition can be built from three steps: feature detection, feature description (ORB binary descriptors), and feature matching with a Hamming-distance brute-force matcher.
A homography maps points on a flat reference surface (z = 0) to the image plane, and it can be estimated from matches with cv2.findHomography using RANSAC.
RANSAC makes homography estimation robust to false matches (outliers) by repeatedly fitting models to random subsets and scoring consistency.
Projecting the reference image corners with cv2.perspectiveTransform shows whether the recognized surface is located correctly in the target frame.
The next step (part 2) extends the homography to project 3D points and draw a 3D model from an .obj file.
summary.summary: The author builds a card-based augmented reality proof of concept in Python and OpenCV. The post walks through recognizing a flat reference surface with ORB features, brute-force Hamming matching with a cross-check, and estimating the surface-to-image homography with RANSAC, including short code snippets and a derivation of the pinhole-camera relation for planar points. It explicitly is not a full tutorial and stops before projecting 3D models, which is deferred to part 2.
